newsitem.title: UK: Salomon recommends UK insurance shares.
newsitem.headline: Salomon recommends UK insurance shares.

text.p: Stockbroker Salomon Brothers said on Monday that the latest evidence on the UK underwriting cycle supported its positive outlook on UK non-life insurance shares.

"We reiterate our case that current share prices more than fully discount the likely decline in earnings and that investors should adopt an overweight stance in the sector," Salomon analysts Andrew Pitt and Trevor May said in a note.
"Excellent interim results and signs of a definite upturn in UK personal lines premium rates now underpin the composite insurers, confirming our optimism about a smoother underwriting cycle."

Premium rates on most types of insurance have been falling for the last two years or more, with private motor leading the way. However, some insurers say they have reversed the trend in private motor in the last few months.
"There is clear evidence that motor insurance rates are rising and that household rates may not be far behind," Salomon said.
Lower first half 1996 results from the four leading UK composite insurers were to be expected, it added.
"This reflects an erosion of the past two years' super-normal profitability rather than any return to the severe losses of the early 1990s."

Salomon said that shares in Royal & Sun Alliance were significantly undervalued and remained its core recommendation with an increased target price of 500 pence. The shares were trading at 396-1/2 at 1329 GMT.
General Accident Plc shares are also rated a buy with a target price of 720 pence, compared with a current 678 pence.
Salomon recommends shares in both Commercial Union Plc and Guardian Royal Exchange (GARD.L, currently trading at 595-1/2 and 254 respectively, as a hold.
"Detailed valuations lend strong support to share prices both in absolute terms and in international comparison," the analysts said.
The only cloud on the horizon was excess capital, which could dilute sector returns on equity if no action is taken, they added.

"However, we believe that, in most cases, sector management is alive to the need for efficient capital allocation...On an 18 month time horizon, we expect all four companies to have laid more detailed expansion plans in front of investors."
